lesson: Keep the signal colour for strokes, underlines, arrows, numbers, and emphasis only, about one red element per scene. Measure the share of each frame covered by each accent, so 'aqua sparingly' and 'red means danger' become checks instead of hopes.

title: In paper styles, text arrives as an object and never fades
lesson: In a paper or print style, text enters physically: typed on, slid in on a strip, stamped, or revealed by an underline swipe. It never fades in, because paper does not fade.

title: One short label per beat, only for a date, a name, or a number
lesson: Allow one label of 1 to 4 words per beat, on a strip or a stamp, and only when the beat carries a date, a name, or a number. Otherwise the picture and the captions carry it.

title: Never put an eye bar or 'redacted' treatment on a real person
lesson: Eye bars, blurs, and 'redacted' stamps on real people, officials, or candidates imply guilt and, on an AI likeness, break the no-synthetic-faces rule. Use them only on code-drawn anonymous silhouettes, to mean 'identity protected'.

title: Draw red string only between documented, sourced links
lesson: Connection lines (red string, arrows) between people or groups must show a documented link, with the source on screen. A conspiracy-board look for undocumented links is a false-light risk and weakens trust.

title: Offer three hooks that open with a number or a date
lesson: When Claude drafts the script, it first offers three opening lines that start with a number or a date, so the hook stat lands in the first 2 seconds.

title: Declare a layout recipe per beat and cap the static ones
lesson: Name each beat's layout recipe and motion treatment in the storyboard. No two beats in a row share a recipe, and static cards or side-by-sides fill at most one third of the beats, so the film does not become a slideshow.

title: Fine texture under a moving camera: coarse dots, fixed to the object
lesson: Halftone dots, paper grain, and hairlines are the first detail lost to scaling and H.264 compression, and under a drifting camera they shimmer. Keep dot pitch at least 6 px at 1080 wide, attach texture to the object (not the screen), and check a platform re-encode before delivery.

title: Keep a written profile per entity and read it before every task
lesson: Put the organization's profile (canonical name, URL, phone, address, taglines, audience, tone) and a never-claim list in one file that every task reads first, so nobody retypes a phone number wrong.

title: QC every piece against the profile, digit for digit, with a reason for every fail
lesson: Before anything ships, check every script line, caption, on-screen line, and end card against the profile and the fact bank: names, URLs, phone numbers, bill numbers, and addresses exactly, plus never-claims and tone. Report pass or fail with the reason for each fail, and review only the failures.

title: Prove a gate works by planting a known-bad item
lesson: Test every check with a deliberately bad input (a false claim, a wrong digit, an unsigned fact) and confirm it fails for the right reason before trusting it on real work.

title: Log every hook and never repeat one
lesson: Give every piece an ID and log its opening line; check each new hook against the log before it is used. Without a log, a series drifts into the same openings in slightly different words.

title: Urgency only from real facts
lesson: Any urgency or scarcity in a script comes from a sourced fact (a hearing date, a vote deadline, a real limit), never from an invented one.

title: No testimonial from someone who did not live it
lesson: A presenter speaks to 'you' as a host or explains; nobody describes results or experiences they did not have. Composites are introduced honestly.

title: Squash a landing about the ground contact, and make it at least 12 percent to read
lesson: Weight on a landing is a squash (wider, shorter) scaled about the point of contact, never about the hip. A 5 percent squash is invisible on a 235 px figure; 14 to 16 percent reads at a glance and recovers in about 0.3 s with a small rebound.

title: Secondary motion in a pure-function-of-time renderer is a time offset, not state
lesson: Cloth and hair that lag the body must not keep state between frames (every frame is seek(t)). Sample the figure's own motion function two to four frames back, take a damped average of the velocity over those frames, and turn it into a swing angle. The lag and the damping fall out of the time offset and the weights.

title: Let the page enumerate what it can draw, and look at a figure sheet after every change
lesson: A contact sheet of every pose, kit, hand state, face and prop at two sizes, labelled, is the fastest way to see a figure change. Have the page list its own POSE, KITS, PROPS_LOOK and expression tables so a new item appears on the next sheet with no edit to the tool, and read the sheet before writing a test.

title: Check a drawn face's style on its pixels: colours, gloss and a rim test tell flat from photo
lesson: A flat face has few colours that together cover nearly all of it, no near-white pixels inside, and no dark ring at the head's edge over a light inside. Measure those three on the real render (faceStyleCheck) and plant a texture, a gloss dot and an outline to prove each fails. Hair and beards are dark on both sides of the rim band, so the rim test compares each rim pixel with the pixel just inside it.

title: With a face on, the hair cap behind the head must take the face's hair colour
lesson: The silhouette rig draws a slightly larger cap behind the head in the figure's back tone; with a skin-toned head that cap reads as a dark helmet rim. Give the cap the face's hair colour as soon as a face is on.

title: Give every prop a size and an anchor, and test flatness by counting colours
lesson: A prop pack is usable from a storyboard only when each prop carries its size, its aspect and the point that stands on the ground, so a scene places it by its feet. Prove the flat style by counting the colours that cover 0.4 percent or more of the drawn pixels: a flat prop has 2 to 5 and they cover over 90 percent; a gradient or a texture breaks both numbers.

title: Decode the vendored TopoJSON in a few lines instead of loading a library for one outline
lesson: The US atlas in engine/vendor is TopoJSON in geographic coordinates: arcs are delta-encoded and quantized by a transform. Twelve lines decode a state's rings; an Albers projection with California's own parallels (34 and 40.5) fits it to a canvas. No d3 or topojson-client is needed for a single outline, so a prop can draw the state anywhere the atlas data is loaded.

title: Map a kit's parts to the rig by joint pairs, and keep the kit's own proportions
lesson: An SVG kit character rides the engine's poses when every part names the two joints it spans (shoulder to elbow, hip to knee, neck to head) in the kit's own coordinates; the loader derives the rig's proportions from those joints and maps each part's native segment onto the posed segment with one translate, rotate and uniform scale. The kit then takes every pose key, the weight keys and the secondary motion with no change to the specs. The segment that places the head must start at the shoulder (neck = shoulder) or the head scales differently from the body.

title: Test an SVG parser against a twin drawn with plain canvas calls, not against itself
lesson: To prove an SVG loader, draw the same shapes with explicit canvas calls (the same rounded-rect cubics, ellipse, polygon and path numbers) under the same joint transforms and compare pixels: zero differing pixels proves the path parser, the transform stack, the fill handling and the placement at once. A golden frame alone would only prove the parser agrees with its past self.

title: A kit's licence is checked in two places and recorded once
lesson: Refuse a kit with no licence text both in the loader (the page never draws it) and in the install tool (nothing is recorded); the install tool writes the asset row with the licence, the author and the parts so kb.py check and the fact that every asset has a licence stay true. No kit is ever downloaded by the engine: a kit is a folder already on disk.

title: Put stills on the review page as short MP4 renders so one page carries the whole review
lesson: The private review page (D-038) plays video renders and takes notes by timestamp; it shows no images. Turn a style frame into a 5 s held still and a tall contact sheet into a slow 24 s pan (ffmpeg loop plus an animated crop), upload them as renders beside the motion test, and the morning approval happens on one page with one set of notes.

title: A style frame stops the figure left of the desk, with the prop's foot on the desk top
lesson: Place every prop by its anchor and compute the desk top from the prop's own geometry before placing anything on it; a figure that walks in stops short of the furniture, never in front of it. The first style frame had the speaker standing in the chair and the document floating 55 px above the desk; both were fixed by anchors and one derived line (deskTop).

title: Export the code-drawn figure as a kit so an illustrator starts from CFC's proportions
lesson: The rig can write itself out as SVG (one named layer per part, a kit.json with the joints) that the kit loader reads straight back; an illustrator redraws inside those layers and the result rides every pose. Two traps: the manifest's height is the figure's own height, not the viewBox (or every limb scales short), and SVG arc caps need sweep flag 0 to bulge outward like the canvas arcs (or every limb loses a half-disc at each end).

title: A group on a slope stops one gap behind the figure ahead
lesson: When several figures climb a path together, give each one a stopping point one gap behind the one ahead (clamp its progress to 1 minus its index times the gap), or the leader stops at the top and the rest bunch into it, which breaks FC-4. A crowd helper needs the same rule in one dimension: a slot at least .42 of the figure height wide, else refuse.

title: A listener's nod must be at least 15 degrees, and a point must end on its object
lesson: On a 440 px figure a 6 degree nod over 0.6 s is invisible on a contact sheet and at full size: use about 15 degrees as a double dip over 0.8 s. A level pointing arm whose line runs to another person's head reads as scolding; aim the point down so the finger ends on the object (the seal), and keep the listener's chin level. A figure that starts inside the frame mid-stride reads as walking across, not in: start off-frame at a natural stride (about 0.6 of the figure height per second).

title: Tie a walking figure's speed to its stride, or the planted foot skates
lesson: A walk cycle moves the stance foot about .38 of the figure height per step; the body must travel the same distance or the foot slides (a treadmill shuffle that a motion critic measures in one frame). Use strideSpeed(h, cycles, k) for the figure's speed, plant the feet (plant: 1) so nothing hovers through the stride, ease the halt over the last step (walkDistance), and mind the bob's sign (+ is down in drawSide).

title: Draw props at the figure's scale: a desk top near .4 of the figure, a seat near .26
lesson: Furniture placed by its anchor still needs its size set against the figure: a desk whose top sits at knee height (.28 h) reads as a coffee table, a chair whose seat is at .19 h as a plinth. Scale the prop so the desk top lands near .4 of the figure height and a seat near .26, and give an upright document a stand.

title: Block and list every request a render does not serve from disk
lesson: During capture, abort every request that the engine's own disk server does not answer, list each one, and fail the render if the list is not empty. No frame may depend on the network.

title: Check that the audio stream and the video stream end together
lesson: At finalize, compare the audio stream's own length with the video stream's, within one frame. The file's total length is not enough.

title: Check free memory before a render and stop below a floor
lesson: Before a render or any other heavy step, read free memory. Below a floor, stop and print the reading instead of starting a render that stalls the Mac. Run one heavy job at a time.

title: Record the master's size and SHA-256, and check every delivered copy against it
lesson: At release, write the master's byte size and SHA-256 into a release record, and check that every delivered copy has the same hash. A file name does not prove which render went out.

title: Offer full-sentence subtitles as a per-project caption style
lesson: Word-timed captions of 2 to 4 words (TC-6) stay the default, but a project may choose sentence subtitles at intake when its style and content call for them: one script sentence per subtitle in a burned-in band, at most two lines, never two at once, on screen for the whole of its sentence. SRT and VTT are still written.

title: Draft small, and batch the fixes when a change re-renders everything
lesson: Draft at 720p with the layout scaled, so the final keeps the draft's line breaks and its contact sheet matches scene for scene. When a pipeline has no per-scene reuse, a one-word fix costs a full render: collect fixes and re-render once.

title: Short function words inside a label lose their stress in the scratch voice
lesson: Kokoro phonemizes with eSpeak NG and has no inline phoneme markup. Unstressed function words ('from', 'as', 'to', 'for', 'in') run into the word before ('New from' heard as 'newfrom'). Check the phonemes with the same package, fix only the spoken text (a comma adds stress and a pause; a respelling such as 'frum' adds stress only), voice two or three takes and let the owner pick by ear. The voice is deterministic.

title: Look a word up by text both the script and the spoken text share
lesson: When a pronunciation table respells a word for the voice, any scene that finds a word's time by its written form fails. Key a lookup to a word that is spelled the same in both texts.

title: A checker rule that blocks an approved change gets a narrow exception
lesson: When a rule blocks a change the owner asked for (an inch value in brackets pushed an approved sentence over 25 words), add a narrow, named exception to the checker (an inch value after a mm value is the same measurement) rather than rewording the approved sentence or weakening the rule.

title: Build tools under the GPL: ask the owner, list them, never ship them
lesson: ffmpeg-static ships a GPL ffmpeg, and the phonemizer bundles eSpeak NG (GPL) though its own licence says Apache-2.0. These are acceptable as build tools that never ship; only their output does. Ask the owner, then list them in the project's licence notes.

title: The owner judges by eye and ear, not by report
lesson: Every gate is a file the owner plays or looks at with the session stopped: the voice samples, the sample scene, the draft, the takes. A report supports the choice; it never replaces seeing and hearing it.

title: Check every kill-list reason against the code, as for a backlog row
lesson: A scoping session's kill list needs the same check as its backlog rows: read the killed lesson in full, then confirm each stated reason in the code before anyone approves the list. Ask the approval question over the whole list, not part of it.

title: Check an outside toolkit report against the knowledge base before building anything from it
lesson: When a research report recommends a stack, map each recommendation to what the engine and the knowledge base already have before adopting any of it. Three of six recommendations already existed, one was split across files, one had already lost two comparisons; only one was a real gap.

title: Before touching a shared checkout, look for commits and file changes from the last few minutes
lesson: An overnight session can still be committing when the morning session starts. Before any git command in a shared checkout, read the last commit's time and the files changed in the last 45 minutes; if another session is live, work in your own worktree on your own branch and leave the merge for when it is done (R-019).

title: Keep every colour, font and type constant in one theme file
lesson: Put the palette, the house colours, the meaning accents, the dark-field accents, the scene fields, the fonts and the type constants in brand/theme.json; the page builder writes it into build/theme.js before lib.js loads, project.py takes the font defaults from it, and lint.py --engine fails a colour literal in engine drawing code. Move values, never change them, so the golden frames prove nothing moved.

title: A scratch voice for timing drafts is marked so it can never ship
lesson: Use a local Kokoro voice only to time drafts and sheets before the staff recording exists; name the file narration_scratch.wav, let the build mark release.scratch_voice, and keep a release gate that fails until a real recording replaces it. Never send a script to a vendor that licenses inputs for this.

title: Render a still at every beat's cue word and look at it before building the next beat
lesson: After each beat, render one frame at its cue word and one half a second later into review/stills/, look at them, and give the critic the same frames. Contact sheets show the whole piece; the beat stills show the moment the type lands, where overlaps and weak heroes hide.

title: Two sessions drawing the same object under one asset name: the later module silently wins
lesson: When parallel sessions add props, a shared registry key (the scene asset layer) lets the module that loads last overwrite the other with no error, and a golden frame is the only thing that notices. Register a pack under its own prefix, never overwrite a name that exists, and check the asset names of both branches before the merge.

title: Open-licence icons become house props through one re-style pass, not by hand
lesson: Build an icon kit with tools/kit_from_icons.py: wrap each icon in one group in the house ink, drop every stroke, per-shape fill, invisible artboard rect and opacity, keep the viewBox, write kit.json with one prop per icon and the licence text beside it, then kit_install.py records it. Phosphor fill icons carry fill=currentColor on the root and some an artboard rect; Material Symbols use a viewBox that starts at -960; both pass the loader unchanged after the pass.

title: Read every vendored licence file once: a download can save an error page under the licence name
lesson: After vendoring a library or data set, open its licence file and read the first line: a fetch that misses can write the server's error message under LICENSE.txt and the folder then looks licensed when it is not. Record the real licence text and the source beside the file.

title: A chart beat shows a bar rising and lands the number as the fact's own text
lesson: Draw charts from facts only: a bar or line rises on its cue word and the numeral lands once the rise is over, as the fact's on-screen text at its final value, so no false intermediate number is ever on screen (R-018). Votes come from one tally fact per chamber (ayes to noes); one accent per card, by meaning. A fact whose text holds digits passes the number rule (a bill number would), so the storyboard reviewer still reads every chart.

title: A hint meant for every build must sit on every build path
lesson: When a measure is printed as a hint for every finished file, put it where every build path passes, not only in the pipeline being worked on. The unchanged-frames share lived only in the one-command narrated-explainer pipeline; a spec build (make_video.py --final) never printed it. explainercheck.py --hint prints the one line and writes nothing; make_video.frozen_hint prints it after every final build, so both paths read the same number.
